label: Daniel (support → founder)
tagline: Twenty years from night-shift support to founder: failed pivots, a famous unread library, and a good ending.

entries.title: Call centre nights
entries.body: Tech support night shifts. Bought my first programming book; it sat unread for a year. Good intentions, dusty shelves.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2006
entries.body: Year 2006: bought more books than I finished reading. Built more than I read. Onward.

entries.title: Bought the canon
entries.body: Bought twelve classic CS books in a sale. Collection growing; finished reading zero. The shelves look impressive though.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2007
entries.body: Year 2007: family steady, shelves fuller, TBR to-read pile taller. The work still got done.

entries.title: First scripts at work
entries.body: Automated my support macros. Bought three scripting books; skimmed one, shelved two unread.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2008
entries.body: Year 2008: a hard pivot year. Bea and June kept me honest; the collection kept growing unread.

entries.title: Pivot attempt one
entries.body: Applied to 40 junior dev jobs, rejected by all. Bought interview-prep books, unread, as motivation furniture.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2009
entries.body: Year 2009: fewer purchases, same pattern. I collect starts; life supplies finishes.

entries.title: Weight and worry
entries.body: Stress eating through layoff rumours. Dad Tom says walk it off. Bought a fitness book; unread, obviously.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2010
entries.body: Year 2010: bought more books than I finished reading. Built more than I read. Onward.

entries.title: Night school code
entries.body: Community college coding nights after shifts. Bought the textbook new; a classmate finished reading it, I carried it.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2011
entries.body: Year 2011: family steady, shelves fuller, TBR to-read pile taller. The work still got done.

entries.title: Sister Bea, anchor
entries.body: Bea proofreads my applications and my life. Family gravity: Sunday calls, no skipping.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2012
entries.body: Year 2012: a hard pivot year. Bea and June kept me honest; the collection kept growing unread.

entries.title: First dev job
entries.body: Junior backend role at last, four years late. Bought five architecture books to celebrate; finished reading none by Christmas.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2013
entries.body: Year 2013: fewer purchases, same pattern. I collect starts; life supplies finishes.

entries.title: Shelf audit
entries.body: Shelf audit: 63 books bought, 9 finished reading. I collect beginnings. The TBR to-read pile is now furniture.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2014
entries.body: Year 2014: bought more books than I finished reading. Built more than I read. Onward.

entries.title: Incidents teach
entries.body: Finding: our outages taught more than any book I bought. Write-ups I actually finished reading, unlike my shelves.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2015
entries.body: Year 2015: family steady, shelves fuller, TBR to-read pile taller. The work still got done.

entries.title: Go, deeply
entries.body: Rewrote the log pipeline in Go. Bought two Go books unread; the docs online did the teaching.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2016
entries.body: Year 2016: a hard pivot year. Bea and June kept me honest; the collection kept growing unread.

entries.title: June Park, meetup
entries.body: Met June at a demo night. She designs; I hoard references. We whiteboarded until the venue closed.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2017
entries.body: Year 2017: fewer purchases, same pattern. I collect starts; life supplies finishes.

entries.title: Pivot: side project
entries.body: Side project: deploy previews. Bought a startup library (11 books, unread) and built instead. Correct order, accidentally.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2018
entries.body: Year 2018: bought more books than I finished reading. Built more than I read. Onward.

entries.title: Startup incorporated
entries.body: Incorporated with June. Ten paying teams. My unread shelf now includes three fundraising books.

entries.title: Runway v1
entries.body: Seven months runway. Bought a finance classic; Bea finished reading it and summarised it for me. System works.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2019
entries.body: Year 2019: family steady, shelves fuller, TBR to-read pile taller. The work still got done.

entries.title: Back, again
entries.body: Couch-coding wrecked my back. Standing desk, walks. Bought an ergonomics book; Alex finished reading his copy.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2020
entries.body: Year 2020: a hard pivot year. Bea and June kept me honest; the collection kept growing unread.

entries.title: Onboarding beats features
entries.body: Churn interviews: teams failed to reach first value. Rebuilt onboarding; activation doubled. No book required.

entries.title: Founder notes Fridays
entries.body: Friday note to June: shipped, learned, avoiding. Shared method. My bookshelf stays unread; my notes get read.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2021
entries.body: Year 2021: fewer purchases, same pattern. I collect starts; life supplies finishes.

entries.title: The pivot conversation
entries.body: Previews are a feature, not the company. Six weeks to validate release-confidence or wind down. Shelves of unread strategy books judged us silently.

entries.title: Release confidence sells
entries.body: Pivot validated. Teams pay to know a release is safe. Positioning simplified in one move.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2022
entries.body: Year 2022: bought more books than I finished reading. Built more than I read. Onward.

entries.title: Seed extension
entries.body: 18 months more runway, no priced round. Bought a negotiation book; still in the wrapper. We negotiated fine anyway.

entries.title: Sleep is the roadmap
entries.body: Five-hour nights made my decisions stupid. No Slack after nine. Bought a sleep book, unread, and just slept.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2023
entries.body: Year 2023: family steady, shelves fuller, TBR to-read pile taller. The work still got done.

entries.title: Enterprise no
entries.body: Three enterprise pilots asked; piloted one, declined two. Focus is the strategy. Bought an enterprise sales book for the shelf museum.

entries.title: Acquisition passes
entries.body: Two acquirers circled; terms wrong, team would scatter. Declined. Bea said the unread books approve of patience.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2024
entries.body: Year 2024: a hard pivot year. Bea and June kept me honest; the collection kept growing unread.

entries.title: Kill criteria early
entries.body: Every bet ships with kill criteria and a date. The pivot took six weeks because past-us wrote the exit.

entries.title: Mentoring founders
entries.body: Accelerator office hours. I lend my unread books with honesty labels: “unread but beloved”. They laugh, then borrow.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2025
entries.body: Year 2025: fewer purchases, same pattern. I collect starts; life supplies finishes.

entries.title: Learned to sell
entries.body: Fifty sales calls. Listen, recap, ask what happens if nothing changes. No sales book finished; the calls taught it.

entries.title: Twenty years of shelves
entries.body: Support desk to founder, one failed pivot, one good one. My shelves hold 200 beginnings; my life finally has middles. It works out.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2026
entries.body: Year 2026: bought more books than I finished reading. Built more than I read. Onward.

entries.title: Drive export: support macros doc (2007)
entries.body: Night-shift macros collected in a doc: the ten replies that solved half the queue. Bought three more books on systems this month; the shelf is outpacing finishing again.

entries.title: Gmail thread: June Park intro (2009)
entries.body: June Park introduced over email by Sam Ortiz after the meetup. June builds support tooling; offered to pair on a queue dashboard prototype.

entries.title: Drive export: night-shift budget (2011)
entries.body: Budget sheet export: overtime in, textbooks out. The unread canon grows: bought the full distributed-systems shelf, finished one of nine.

entries.title: Apple Health export summary (2012)
entries.body: Health export: sleep averaging 5h40m during night shifts, steps low on workdays. Weekend morning runs are the only steady activity.

entries.title: Calendar export: founder Fridays (2014)
entries.body: Recurring Friday block with Alex Kim: prototype review, one metric, no slides. The calendar shows fourteen weeks without a miss.

entries.title: GitHub export: queue triage playbook (2015)
entries.body: Open-sourced playbook from the repo: label first, reply second, escalate with a summary. Three teams forked it in the first month.

entries.title: Slack export: #support-eng thread (2016)
entries.body: Thread with Felix Wagner: macros cut handle time 30 percent; the write-up earned a shout-out in the all-hands notes.

entries.title: LinkedIn export: Grace Nolan message (2017)
entries.body: Grace Nolan hires support engineers; connected after the meetup talk. She likes decision-story portfolios. Follow up with the playbook link.

entries.title: X export: shelves thread (2018)
entries.body: Posted the shelf photo thread: forty-one bought, nine finished. Replies called it a museum of intentions; the cartography of curiosity continues.

entries.title: Family export: Dad Tom care schedule (2019)
entries.body: Shared doc: hospital visiting rota for Dad Tom with Sister Bea, medication list attached, discharge questions for Friday.

entries.title: Contacts export: June Park card (2020)
entries.body: Contact card: June Park, support tooling, prefers async messages. Collaborator since 2009, co-founder conversations since 2019.

entries.title: Notion export: founder thesis (2021)
entries.body: Goal page in Notion: quit the support ladder, build the queue tool shops ask for, sell to ten teams before hiring. Pivot notes from three failed attempts attached.

entries.title: Gmail export: first investor update (2022)
entries.body: Investor update sent by email: two paying teams, churn zero, runway fourteen months. The museum shelf finally has a finished shelf beside it.

entries.title: Apple Health export summary (2023)
entries.body: Health export: sleep back to 7h10m as a founder with no night shifts; morning runs three times a week. The pivot shows in the data first.

entries.title: Drive export: hiring lessons (2024)
entries.body: Findings doc: hire for writing samples, not interviews. The playbook chapter on triage became the onboarding week-one read.

entries.title: Calendar export: sister call Sundays (2025)
entries.body: Sunday call block with Sister Bea kept for six years: family first, then the week. The thread that never went quiet.

entries.title: First computer, second-hand
entries.body: A second-hand PC and a dial-up tone like a doorbell. Took it apart twice before I dared switch it on.

entries.title: Fixed the neighbours' PCs
entries.body: Word got around: the kid on the street fixes computers. Payment in cake, cables, and one memorable lasagne.

entries.title: Glasses for the screen glare
entries.body: Eye test after headaches at the monitor: first glasses. The world, and the code, both got sharper.

entries.title: LAN nights with Alex
entries.body: Summer of borrowed hubs and too-long cables with Alex Kim. We learned networking by breaking it nightly.

entries.title: Paper round and PC fund
entries.body: Paper round money into a jar labelled, without irony, 'RAM'. First lesson in saving for parts.

entries.title: School IT prize letter
entries.body: Letter from school: prize for rebuilding the library PCs over half-term. Filed it like a first pay cheque.

entries.title: Decided: computers, somehow
entries.body: No clear plan, just certainty: work should involve machines and the people stuck with them.

entries.title: First script that saved an hour
entries.body: Wrote a tiny script to rename a term's worth of files. An hour saved; a vocation found.

entries.title: Night-owl term
entries.body: Sleep slid later all term: screens after midnight, mornings like weather. First lesson in what nights cost.

entries.title: Weekend repair jobs
entries.body: Weekend repair jobs for half the street. Kept a notebook of faults and fixes — my first ticket queue.

entries.title: Support job offer letter
entries.body: Offer letter for a night-shift support role. Read it twice, bought an alarm clock the same day.

entries.title: Year-end reflection 2005
entries.body: Year 2005: school done, toolbox full, first real job waiting. The jar labelled RAM is empty and the PC is not.

entries.title: Health record (2006)
entries.body: Night-shift year one: sleep in two blocks, sunglasses on the morning bus. The rota is the health record.

entries.title: Health record (2007)
entries.body: Check-up: all routine. Started walking the long way home after shifts to see daylight on purpose.

entries.title: Health record (2008)
entries.body: Eye strain term: monitor breaks and a desk lamp; headaches eased within weeks.

entries.title: Health record (2009)
entries.body: Vaccination record updated at the clinic; flu jab between night shifts.

entries.title: Health record (2010)
entries.body: Back twinges from the headset chair; a standing desk made from crates, then a real one.

entries.title: Health record (2011)
entries.body: Sleep experiment: no tickets after midnight on days off. Rest improved; so did patience.

entries.title: Health record (2012)
entries.body: Check-up and blood tests: cholesterol watched, everything else steady.

entries.title: Health record (2013)
entries.body: Couch-to-5k finished along the canal, headphones full of support podcasts.

entries.title: Health record (2014)
entries.body: Dental check-up and a crown. Paid in instalments, filed under founder tax: teeth.

entries.title: Health record (2015)
entries.body: First export year: step records begin, averaging 5,800 steps — nights are sedentary and it shows.

entries.title: Health record (2016)
entries.body: Health export summary: steps up on office days, sleep averaging 6h 31m. Nights still audible in the data.

entries.title: Health record (2017)
entries.body: Check-up: blood pressure fine, vitamin D low. Daylight lamp joined the desk.

entries.title: Health record (2018)
entries.body: Swimming term before shifts; sleep deepest on swim weeks.

entries.title: Health record (2019)
entries.body: Health export summary: resting heart rate steadier since the rota changed; sleep nearing seven hours.

entries.title: Health record (2020)
entries.body: Remote year: home desk, daily walks, anxious sleep in the spring. Movement kept the routine honest.

entries.title: Health record (2021)
entries.body: Vaccination course completed; appointments logged with the export.

entries.title: Health record (2022)
entries.body: Founder-year check-up: stress named, walking meetings adopted, blood pressure stable.
